source: 10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-20-0614; PMID32299817; author-labelled EMC patient4 after neoadjuvant radiotherapy from reused R3 primary gate
new_route: Crossref publisher-deposited article-PDF URL, not the previously failed AACR landing page; one ordinary public file request, no UI or private access
question: Does the post-radiotherapy EMC microdose case provide an informative local drug-versus-vehicle apoptosis contrast or differential compound effect that the original feasibility interpretation and existing USZ/NCC observations did not already answer?
rationale: A directly measured fresh-patient tissue condition would be different from proliferating cell-line ATP screens; local vehicle and drug-distribution controls could discriminate measured apoptosis from treatment-associated background.
mechanism: Local pharmacodynamic apoptosis, conditional on assay specificity and intratumoral drug distribution; no pathway dependency or clinical efficacy inference
comparators: All reported patient4 drugs/doses, local vehicle/uninjected tissue, measured distribution and published treatment/tissue conditions; other patients are context, not EMC donors
strongest_alternative: Prior radiation, spatial necrosis/immune composition, local exposure or the primary paper's already reported feasibility result accounts for the measurement. A recovered paper detail alone has no new scientific value.
defeat: No primary EMC identity/control crosswalk; unavailable quantitative assay/control values; no independent empirical contrast; or the original publication already answers the useful question. Retain any recovered observations descriptively and do not promote.
future_validation: Only if an unanswered robust contrast survives would adequate independent authentic EMC tissue/model and controls be required; existing screens are donor-level context, not interchangeable exposure assays.
limit: Initial pilot deadline11:01UTC,64MiB raw softcap, no additional route after an ordinary-file access failure without new discriminating rationale
